justification: every intended dependency is implied by an adjudicated key and no intended multivalued dependency remains, with no candidate left unruled

subject: model
value: One row is the full extracted plain-text body of one catalogued document, held in a 1:1 vertical partition so the large text stays out of the metadata row.
justification: DDL: doc_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES documents(id) ON DELETE CASCADE. That is simultaneously the declared key and the only observed UCC, and the cascade makes the row's existence dependent on its parent document, so doc_id identifies the row in every legal state. Row counts match exactly (1457 document_text rows against 1457 documents, zero orphans on a left join). The repository MANIFEST describes this catalog family as 'documents + 1:1 document_text split (6NF-style vertical partition for the large text), empty duplicate_sets', which is exactly what the DDL encodes. The packet lists no atomicity candidates and no MVD subjects; the single FD doc_id -> text is key-driven, and text is one archived document body - the extraction of a single PDF - not several instances of one fact. Scope is current-state, inherited from the partition's parent: text is re-extracted from the file at documents.path, so replacing that PDF yields the same doc_id with different text. Nothing is append-only or versioned - there is no extraction-run, timestamp, or version column here, unlike the same-family polytwister-papers catalog which carries a separate text_extractions table.

subject: disposition
justification: 1 adjudicated dependency(ies) violate 3NF under the approved keys: source_subgroup -> source_group. Nothing regenerates this database -- it has no builder and is its own source of truth -- so unlike the generated catalogues the update anomalies are real and the redundancy can drift. Fixing it means migrating the file in place with a lossless proof and a compatibility view, which has not been done. This is the exemption most worth revisiting. Its document-valued columns (author, inferred_author, original_author) were separately accepted and are not what blocks it.

subject: *all-unruled*
justification: documents has 149 rows across 34 columns. At that shape a composite determinant partitions the rows so finely that it determines almost anything, so the observed dependencies not individually ruled are artifacts of this instance rather than statements about the design. Ruled accidental as a set; any one of them can be reopened individually with evidence.

subject: filename
justification: 149 distinct in 149 rows, but paths span .local/tiling, .local/geometry/Zorin, .local/references/research-pdfs and .local/uncategorized, so equal basenames in different directories are possible. The schema declares UNIQUE on path alone — evidence this uniqueness is corpus accident.
Declared PRIMARY KEY. Surrogate identity of the catalogued document; owns every attribute by definition.

subject: original_filename
justification: Pre-intake name (e.g. arXiv ids). Unique here by accident of intake; nothing prevents two sources sharing an original filename.

subject: original_path
justification: Historical intake location. Unique in this corpus only; not declared UNIQUE and not the identity the catalogue keys on.
Declared UNIQUE NOT NULL. The current on-disk location is the natural key of a catalogue row; one file at one path is one document.

subject: sha256 -> source_group,source_subgroup,topic,suggested_folder
justification: Near-key at 148 distinct values in 149 rows. duplicate_sets exists precisely because identical bytes can sit at multiple paths, and nothing forces two copies into the same subgroup or topic — the corpus's one duplicate pair (Smith, chiral aperiodic monotile) simply happens to be co-located. Byte-content genuinely determining size_bytes/pages/text_chars is true of the world but is untestable here on a single repeated hash.

subject: source_subgroup -> source_group
justification: a subgroup belongs to exactly one group: a two-level hierarchy over the source collections, held once per document instead of once.

subject: standard_filename
justification: Derived '<year> - <author> - <title>' rendering. Near-key by construction from other near-unique fields, not an owning entity.

subject: suggested_folder
justification: Derived output of (source_group, source_subgroup, topic), so it cannot be the owner of its own inputs; and the legacy values 'research-pdfs' and '.local/references/research-pdfs' do not follow the <group>/<subgroup>/<topic> prefix rule, so suggested_folder -> source_group holds for those 8 rows purely by luck.

subject: suggested_name
justification: Derived rename target. Unique across these 149 rows but unconstrained; a collision is a rename bug, not a schema guarantee.

subject: text_path
justification: Derived sidecar path, unique only because path is unique in this corpus. A near-key, not an owner.

subject: topic
justification: Subject facet vs. provenance. topic -> source_group holds only because 'computer-graphics-reference' happens to cover exactly the 5 reference-manuals rows; a graphics-reference research PDF or a tiling reference manual breaks it.

subject: model
value: One PDF file currently present in the DAFX corpus tree, with its filesystem facts, pdfinfo metadata, text-extraction outcome, and the derived title/author/year inference plus rename-and-relocation suggestion for it.
justification: DDL declares id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY and path TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE (backed by sqlite_autoindex_documents_1). Those are the only identifying columns. sha256 is deliberately non-unique: documents_sha256_idx is a plain, non-UNIQUE index, and duplicate_sets(sha256 PRIMARY KEY, count, paths_json) exists precisely to record one hash held by several paths. The sibling research-pdfs catalog, same schema family, has 149 documents over 148 distinct sha256 and a populated duplicate_sets row with count=2 - so sha256 being unique across these 1457 rows is a property of this corpus, not of the design. filename, suggested_name, standard_filename, original_filename, original_path and text_path are all derived from path (DAFX proceedings filenames are year-prefixed), and nothing declares any of them unique. Every compound uniqueness subject rides on a near-unique high-cardinality column - inferred_title 1452/1457 distinct, size_bytes 1456, text_chars 1446, title 1365, creation_date 1342 - so they are counting artifacts, accidental. Scope is current-state: path, size_bytes, sha256, pages and text_chars describe the file as last scanned. There is no build_info/metadata/build_inputs table (the same-family polytwister-papers catalog has them), and the enrichment columns were appended by ALTER TABLE onto existing rows, so this catalog is updated in place, not regenerated. path -> sha256 holds for the current snapshot only.

subject: model
value: One row is one content hash for which the scan found more than one file in the catalogued tree, recording how many files share it and which paths they are.
justification: The table is empty here, so the packet's declared_constraints list is blank; I take the key from the DDL text itself - sha256 TEXT PRIMARY KEY - confirmed by sqlite_autoindex_duplicate_sets_1 in sqlite_master, following the instruction to prefer what the DDL declares even where SQLite does not enforce it. One hash is one duplicate group, so sha256 identifies the row in every legal state; count and paths_json are both facts about that group. A populated example exists in the identical-schema research-pdfs catalog: sha256 1a1c2123c63f, count 2, paths_json a JSON array of the two colliding PDF paths. That row also settles what paths_json means: it is a repeating group holding several instances of one fact (a member path), with count being simply its length, so the normalized form is duplicate_set_member(sha256, path) and count becomes derived. paths_json is not in atomicity_candidates because there were zero rows to profile, so I record the finding here rather than as a column verdict. Scope is current-state: this is a derived duplicate index over the paths currently in documents and must be recomputed whenever a file is added, removed, or moved.
